# Reconstructed brain benchmarks

The current results use **39,533 reference nuclei**, 20 reference donors, 40 training donors and 40 evaluation donors, with 2,000 genes and seven cell types. Every primary experiment was rerun from the reconstructed numerical inputs; v16 adds diagnostics without changing those fits.

## Obtain and verify inputs

```bash
python3 reproduction/reproduce.py brain-prepare
```

This extracts the four verified input objects and their manifests into `work/ReconstructedData/`. The [download](../downloads/reconstructed_brain_inputs.zip) is also available directly. These objects generated the current paper; no historical clustering checkpoint is needed.

The source study is [Mathys et al.](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cell.2023.08.039). Download the nine processed Seurat objects from the [AD/Aging Brain Atlas](https://compbio.mit.edu/ad_aging_brain/). To independently reproduce and compare every training/evaluation aggregate and reference block from these source objects:

```bash
Rscript work/ReconstructedData/verify_source_aggregation.R work/ReconstructedData /path/to/ROSMAP_AD
```

The verifier uses the new frozen nucleus selections, reads source objects one at a time and compares exact numerical content. The full source files occupy approximately 174 GiB and require substantial RAM. This verification was completed successfully for the reconstructed version. The downloaded input archive also allows native reruns without rereading those large source files.

## Run the analyses

```bash
python3 reproduction/reproduce.py brain-run
```

The driver installs the archived inference source into a separate library, then runs preflight, direct inference, scorer development, continuous associations, nominated eQTL simulation, standard BayesPrism and paper-output preparation. The configuration is `work/ReconstructedData/config.R`; output is a new `rerun_results` folder within the extracted input directory. Parts are also independently callable as documented in its README. Use separate output directories for changed inputs or methods.

The 39-donor continuous-phenotype analysis retains the previous donor-index-3 sensitivity policy. Expression and eQTL benchmarks retain all original evaluation donors. The new null-stability audit identifies an additional influential profile pattern involving donor 38; this diagnostic does not remove another donor from primary analyses.

## Historical reconstruction audit

The historical clustering workflow in `reproduction/brain/preprocessing/` targets the earlier input version. Its October 18 audit reproduced evaluation counts, but training/reference selections differed. The paper was subsequently rerun using explicitly frozen, independently verified reconstructed selections. Historical signatures are retained for provenance and must not be used to certify the current input version. Current reproduction uses the `ReconstructedData` archive and its source verifier above.

## BayesPrism preprocessing


The current comparison uses BayesPrism 2.2.3, pooled raw reference counts, one state per type and its `GEP` input interface. It applies `cleanup.genes()` with human groups `Rb`, `Mrp`, `other_Rb` and `chrM`, `exp.cells = 1`, followed by `new.prism()` with `outlier.cut = 0.01`, `outlier.fraction = 0.1` and `pseudo.min = 1e-8`. The chain length is 1,000, with 500 burn-in iterations and thinning of two; the full update is run.

There is **no BayesPrism output selection**. Profiles removed by native input QC are tracked explicitly in Table S19. Missing tests remain in the fixed BH family as p = 1 before being reported as unavailable. The common-panel expression comparison uses only shared retained genes, while recall denominators preserve the original target definition.

## Continuous-trait sensitivity

The 39-donor analysis removes original donor 3 from all continuous-trait signal and null tests after identifying its influence. It preserves the original simulated trait values, expression inference and selection ranking, then recomputes the associations on the remaining donors. Table S25 retains the full-cohort comparison and diagnostics. This is a post hoc sensitivity analysis; improvement after removal does not by itself justify excluding a donor in a future biological study. Neither the separate expression/eQTL cohorts nor the independent synthetic-cohort benchmark uses that exclusion.

The code in this branch has been packaged and its entry points checked. This book release does not claim a new full run from the original prepared brain-study inputs. The completed manuscript tables remain available for [saved-data reproduction](reproduce.qmd).
